quests.instruction: The tough, seedy middle of an apple that you usually toss away is called its ___. What word fits?
quests.question: Core
quests.hint: This word names the part shaped a bit like a small hourglass inside the fruit.
quests.explanation: You found it! The tough, seedy middle of an apple you toss away is called its core!
quests.funFact: Sliced open, this part often looks a little like a small hourglass or star shape!

quests.instruction: A lime is divided inside into small, sour ___, just like its bigger citrus cousins. What's the word?
quests.question: Segment
quests.hint: This is the word for each individual section found inside a citrus fruit.
quests.explanation: Exactly right! The small, sour sections inside a lime are called segments!
quests.funFact: Even the smallest citrus fruits still grow with this same natural, sectioned design!

quests.instruction: Removing a coconut's tough, fibrous ___ is the very first step before reaching its hard inner shell. What's the word?
quests.question: Husk
quests.hint: This word names the very first, toughest layer you'd need to strip away from a coconut.
quests.explanation: Wonderful! The very first, toughest layer stripped away from a coconut is its husk!
quests.funFact: Some coconuts are sold with this tough layer already removed, showing just the hard shell!

quests.instruction: The part of an apple that holds the seeds, usually left uneaten, is called its ___. Which word fits?
quests.question: Core
quests.hint: This is the word for the central part, distinct from the skin and the flesh around it.
quests.explanation: Terrific! The part of an apple that holds the seeds, usually left uneaten, is called its core!
quests.funFact: A special little tool exists just for removing this part in one quick motion!

quests.instruction: A papaya's soft orange inside, surrounding its rows of little black seeds, is its ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Flesh
quests.hint: This word describes the soft part making up the bulk of what you eat.
quests.explanation: Yes! A papaya's soft orange inside, around its rows of seeds, is its flesh!
quests.funFact: This soft part can help settle an upset tummy in a papaya especially!

quests.instruction: The dry, papery outer layer sometimes found on nuts and certain fruits is called their ___. What word names it?
quests.question: Husk
quests.hint: This word describes a dry, protective outer covering on certain foods.
quests.explanation: That's right! The dry, papery outer layer found on nuts and certain fruits is called their husk!
quests.funFact: This same word applies to coverings on several different plant foods, not just coconuts!

quests.instruction: An orange naturally splits apart into juicy little sections called ___. What's the word for each of these sections?
quests.question: Segment
quests.hint: This word names each juicy little section inside a citrus fruit.
quests.explanation: Great job! The juicy little sections an orange naturally splits into are called segments!
quests.funFact: Citrus fruits naturally grow with these built-in sections, all covered by one peel!

quests.instruction: Olives and dates both have a single tough ___ running through their center. What's the word?
quests.question: Pit
quests.hint: This is the word for the one hard part, not many small soft ones.
quests.explanation: You got it! Olives and dates both have a single tough pit through their center, matching this word!
quests.funFact: This tough part is exactly what makes pitted versions of these fruits handy for snacking!

quests.instruction: The bright covering pulled away from a banana before you take a bite is called its ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Peel
quests.hint: This is the layer you remove first, before any fruit reaches your mouth.
quests.explanation: Well done! The bright covering pulled away from a banana before eating is called its peel!
quests.funFact: Its bright color actually changes to yellow or brown as the fruit ripens!

quests.instruction: Before you can crack a coconut's hard shell, you must first remove its thick, fibrous ___. Which word fits?
quests.question: Husk
quests.hint: This word names the tough, fibrous layer found on the very outside of a coconut.
quests.explanation: Correct! The thick, fibrous layer removed before cracking a coconut's shell is its husk!
quests.funFact: Removing this tough outer layer is usually the hardest part of opening a fresh coconut!

quests.instruction: A watermelon's tough, thick green outer shell is called its ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Rind
quests.hint: This word names a thick, tough outer layer, tougher than a banana's thin covering.
quests.explanation: Super! A watermelon's tough, thick green outer shell is called its rind!
quests.funFact: Some people surprisingly pickle this tough outer part instead of tossing it away!

quests.instruction: Avocados are famous for their one giant ___ sitting right in the middle. What's the word?
quests.question: Pit
quests.hint: This word names the single large, round part found in the fruit's center.
quests.explanation: Nice work! Avocados are famous for one giant pit in the middle, matching this word!
quests.funFact: This giant round part can sometimes be sprouted in water to grow a brand new plant!

quests.instruction: The center of an apple, which holds its little brown seeds, is known as its ___. What word names it?
quests.question: Core
quests.hint: This word describes the part right in the middle, not the skin or the juicy flesh.
quests.explanation: You found it! The center of an apple that holds its little brown seeds is known as its core!
quests.funFact: This part is tougher than the rest of the fruit, which is why it's often left uneaten!

quests.instruction: A watermelon's sweet, juicy red inside is known as its ___. What word fits?
quests.question: Flesh
quests.hint: This is the part that makes up almost all of what you actually eat.
quests.explanation: Exactly right! A watermelon's sweet, juicy red inside is known as its flesh!
quests.funFact: This soft part is usually the biggest portion of a fruit by far!

quests.instruction: Strawberries carry their tiny ___ on the outside, unlike most other fruits. What's the word for these tiny parts?
quests.question: Seed
quests.hint: This word describes the smallest part of a fruit that holds a new plant waiting to grow.
quests.explanation: Wonderful! Strawberries carry their tiny seeds on the outside, which is exactly what this word names!
quests.funFact: Strawberries are famous for wearing their seeds on the outside instead of hiding them inside!

quests.instruction: The soft green inside of a kiwi, surrounding its tiny black seeds, is called its ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Flesh
quests.hint: This word names the soft part between a fruit's skin and its core or pit.
quests.explanation: Terrific! The soft green inside of a kiwi, around its tiny seeds, is called its flesh!
quests.funFact: This part changes color and softens as a fruit ripens on the plant!

quests.instruction: A honeydew melon's smooth, pale outer shell is called its ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Rind
quests.hint: This is the tough outer layer that protects a melon's soft insides.
quests.explanation: Yes! A honeydew melon's smooth, pale outer shell is called its rind!
quests.funFact: This tough layer is one reason melons can travel long distances without bruising!

quests.instruction: The thick, fibrous outer covering of a coconut, removed before you reach its hard shell, is its ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Husk
quests.hint: This word names a thick, fibrous outer covering, tougher than a simple peel.
quests.explanation: That's right! The thick, fibrous outer covering of a coconut is its husk!
quests.funFact: This fibrous outer part of a coconut can be turned into rope, mats, and even mattress stuffing!

quests.instruction: The outer covering you strip off a mandarin before splitting it into pieces is its ___. What word fits?
quests.question: Peel
quests.hint: This word describes the outer layer that comes off easily without a knife.
quests.explanation: Great job! The outer covering stripped off a mandarin before splitting it is its peel!
quests.funFact: Mandarins are prized because their outer covering comes off so easily by hand!

quests.instruction: Quinces have a tough, seedy ___ in the middle, much like an apple does. What's the word?
quests.question: Core
quests.hint: This word names the firm, seedy middle shared by apples, pears, and quinces.
quests.explanation: You got it! Quinces have a tough, seedy core in the middle, much like an apple does!
quests.funFact: This part helps protect a fruit's seeds until they're ready to be planted!

quests.instruction: An apple's small, woody top piece, which once connected it to its tree, is its ___. What word fits?
quests.question: Stem
quests.hint: This is the small part on top of an apple, once joined to its branch.
quests.explanation: Well done! An apple's small, woody top piece once connected to its tree is its stem!
quests.funFact: This little woody part is usually the first thing to snap off when a fruit is picked!

quests.instruction: A pear's woody little connector at its narrow top is known as its ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Stem
quests.hint: This word names the small woody part at the top of many tree fruits.
quests.explanation: Correct! A pear's woody little connector at its narrow top is known as its stem!
quests.funFact: This small woody part is one clue that a fruit was picked, rather than fallen on its own!

quests.instruction: The leafy green covering wrapped around an ear of corn is called its ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Husk
quests.hint: This word can also describe a leafy wrapping found on some other plant foods.
quests.explanation: Super! The leafy green covering wrapped around an ear of corn is called its husk!
quests.funFact: This word can describe outer coverings on more than just one kind of plant food!

quests.instruction: A citrus fruit's very outermost tough layer, sitting beneath which the peel and pith rest, is sometimes called its ___. What's the word?
quests.question: Rind
quests.hint: This word describes a tough outer protective layer found on melons and some citrus fruits.
quests.explanation: Nice work! A citrus fruit's outermost tough protective layer is sometimes called its rind!
quests.funFact: This same word can describe tough outer coverings on both melons and citrus fruits!

quests.instruction: A pomelo's extra-large sections, each one a juicy ___, are bigger than an orange's. What's the word?
quests.question: Segment
quests.hint: This word names each natural juicy division found inside a citrus fruit.
quests.explanation: You found it! A pomelo's extra-large juicy divisions are called segments!
quests.funFact: A pomelo is one of the biggest citrus fruits, so each of these sections is extra large too!

quests.instruction: The hard, patterned outer shell of a cantaloupe is known as its ___. What word fits?
quests.question: Rind
quests.hint: This word describes a thick, protective outer layer, usually too tough to eat.
quests.explanation: Exactly right! The hard, patterned outer shell of a cantaloupe is known as its rind!
quests.funFact: This tough outer layer protects the soft, juicy fruit inside from bumps and bruises!

quests.instruction: Apples and watermelons both have small dark ___ scattered inside their juicy flesh. What's the word?
quests.question: Seed
quests.hint: This word names the tiny part a brand new plant could grow from.
quests.explanation: Wonderful! Apples and watermelons both have small dark seeds scattered inside their flesh, which is exactly what this word names!
quests.funFact: A tiny one of these can grow into a whole new fruit tree or vine!

quests.instruction: Apricots have one smooth, hard ___ inside, just like their bigger peach cousins. What word names it?
quests.question: Pit
quests.hint: This word describes a single hard part, unlike the many soft seeds in an apple.
quests.explanation: Terrific! Apricots have one smooth, hard pit inside, just like peaches, matching this word!
quests.funFact: The seed hiding inside an apricot's hard part even looks a little like a tiny almond!

quests.instruction: A mandarin can be pulled apart into several small, curved ___. What word names these small pieces?
quests.question: Segment
quests.hint: This word describes the natural little wedges found inside citrus fruits.
quests.explanation: Yes! The small, curved pieces a mandarin pulls apart into are called segments!
quests.funFact: This natural design makes citrus fruits especially easy to share with friends!

quests.instruction: Pumpkins and cucumbers are both packed with rows of flat, oval ___. What word names them?
quests.question: Seed
quests.hint: This word describes the flat, oval bits found in the center of many fruits.
quests.explanation: That's right! Pumpkins and cucumbers are both packed with rows of flat, oval seeds, matching this word!
quests.funFact: Some of these flat, oval bits can even be roasted into a tasty snack!
